lines.text: The oldest living cultures on Earth, then convict ships, gold, war and a new nation. This is the story of Australia, from its First Peoples to today.
Long before any people, the layers of a great red rock were laid down in the heart of the continent. Uluru is sacred to the Anangu people.
At least fifty thousand years ago, people reached Australia. Their descendants became hundreds of nations, with cultures among the oldest living in the world.
About forty-two thousand years ago, people at Lake Mungo buried their dead, among the oldest human remains found in Australia.
Then, in 1770, the British naval officer James Cook sailed up the east coast and charted it for the first time.
Eleven ships left Britain in 1787 to found a penal colony. In January 1788 the First Fleet reached Botany Bay.
They settled at Sydney Cove. The convict colony grew into Sydney, Australia's largest city, with its harbour and bridge.
From the start, settlers and Aboriginal peoples fought over the land, in frontier wars that went on for more than a century.
In 1835 Melbourne was founded on the south coast. It would grow rich on gold.
Edmund Barton, born in 1849, would lead the movement to unite the colonies and become the first prime minister.
In 1851 gold was found in New South Wales and Victoria. Migrants poured in, many from China, and the colonies grew fast.
At Ballarat in 1854, miners rose against licence fees and harsh policing. Troops stormed their stockade, but the protest won reform.
In 1882 Australia beat England at cricket in England. A newspaper declared English cricket dead, and the Ashes were born.
John Curtin, born in 1885, would lead Australia through most of the Second World War.
On the first day of 1901, six British colonies came together as one country, and Australia was born.
One of the new nation's first laws kept non-white migrants out. The White Australia policy lasted until the seventies.
Federation gave Australia a constitution, a national parliament and a government of its own, still within the British Empire.
From the early nineteen hundreds, governments took Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children from their families. They became the Stolen Generations.
Don Bradman, born in 1908, would finish with a Test batting average of just under one hundred, the best the game has seen.
In 1913 work began on a new capital, Canberra, a compromise between rival Sydney and Melbourne, designed by Walter Burley Griffin.
In 1915 Australians landed at Gallipoli in the Allied attempt to take the Dardanelles. It failed, and is remembered every year.
In 1920 an airline was founded in Queensland. Qantas became Australia's national carrier.
In 1942, on the Kokoda Track in New Guinea, Australian soldiers stopped the Japanese advance.
In 1956 Melbourne became the first city in the southern hemisphere to host the Olympics.
Anthony Albanese, born in Sydney in 1963, would lead Labor and become prime minister in 2022.
In 1967 more than nine in ten voters agreed to count Aboriginal people in the census and let the nation make laws for them.
Cathy Freeman, born in 1973, would grow up to be one of Australia's greatest sprinters.
That same year the Sydney Opera House opened on the harbour, its white roofs like sails.
And in Sydney, the brothers Malcolm and Angus Young formed AC DC, whose Back in Black became one of the best-selling albums ever.
In 1975 most of the Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system on Earth, became a marine park.
In 1992, in the Mabo case, the High Court recognised native title and threw out the idea that the land had belonged to no one.
In 1996 a gunman killed thirty-five people at Port Arthur in Tasmania. Australia answered with strict gun laws.
In 2000 Sydney hosted the Olympics. Cathy Freeman lit the flame and then won the four hundred metres.
In 2008 Prime Minister Kevin Rudd stood in Parliament and formally apologised to the Stolen Generations.
And in the Black Summer of 2019, the worst bushfires on record burned more than twenty million hectares.
From the oldest living cultures to a modern nation, Australia's story is still being told.
